rubric_items.reason: Found the main issue: more data is exposed under the MVP grant-all identity. It also checks that the lateral join's values are bound parameters and that React escapes the output. No route is new or unreported, and I saw no injection.

Findings point at the right lines in the changed code (patientRepo.ts L123/L129, PatientsPage.tsx L15). But pack_sha pins the base SHA while those lines exist only at head_sha, and C4 cites a restated claim instead of code.
Rating SF-1 minor fits an MVP where every request is granted and the question goes to a human. SF-2 is a robustness note more than a security weakness, and minor is the right ceiling for it.

Both findings give a fix direction. SF-1's 'keep it behind the same permission' is already true (patients:read), so the only real action is to restrict access once sign-in exists. SF-2's 'existing error path' is an API error format that the web page cannot use.
No real false positives. SF-2 (silent fallback to the default time zone) is borderline as a security finding, but it is marked minor and its claims are accurate.

findings.text: Code citations use the `sample-system:` prefix and pack_sha pins base SHA 415369…. The cited lines (lateral join L123/L129, startsAt fallback L15) exist only at impl head_sha e0527287…, so the anchors do not hold at the pinned SHA.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the review's code citations to impl head_sha (or record head_sha in pack_sha) so that the line anchors resolve.

findings.text: SF-1's fix says to 'keep it behind the same permission as the list'. The GET / route already declares requirePermission('patients:read'), so that part of the fix does nothing. The only real action is to restrict access once sign-in exists.

cites.quote: keep it behind the same permission as the list and restrict once sign-in exists (Q-01)

findings.suggested_fix: Say that the route already requires patients:read, and make the fix direction 'enforce the real patients:read check when sign-in replaces identify/requirePermission'.

findings.text: SF-2 says to surface the invalid setting through the 'existing error path' and backs this with C3. C3 is the API's JSON error format (ValidationError). The fallback runs client-side in PatientsPage, so that path does not apply.

cites.quote: the existing error format is JSON with field messages (C3), so a settings problem has a place to be reported

Invalid input is 400 with one
message per field (`ValidationError`)

findings.suggested_fix: Point SF-2's fix at a client-side channel (for example a console warning or a settings banner), or validate HOSPITAL_TZ when the server starts.

findings.text: C4 cites impl.md#L66, which is just the impl's own claim restating the design. It is not the code that adds the field. Patient data exposure is the main finding, so this claim should point directly at the code.

cites.quote: next_appointment: r.next_id === null || r.next_starts_at === null || r.next_doctor_name === null
In the MVP every request is the actor `staff` and every permission is granted.
never request bodies, contact details or medical
The design's list item addition is `next_appointment`, an object or null.
{ id: r.next_id, starts_at: r.next_starts_at.toISOString(), doctor_name: r.next_doctor_name }
